name: Off-Highway Vehicle
description: A motorized vehicle not designed for highway use and capable of cross-country travel; an off-road e-moto is a class I off-highway vehicle, a two-wheeler with a straddle seat and handlebars that doesn't qualify as road capable. Defined by North Dakota Century Code §39-29-01 and regulated by chapter 39-29.

restrictions.rule: Not designed for highway use and capable of cross-country travel; electric bicycles are excluded
Class I: a seat or saddle the rider straddles, handlebars steering two wheels, and not road capable under the equipment laws

Registered with the Department of Transportation for two years, with a reflective decal or a plate displayed: a $5 fee plus a $15 trail tax; not needed on private land alone or for organized track racing
One registered in another state needs a $10-a-year out-of-state public trails and lands access permit

Riders must carry a driver's license or permit; a rider under 16 without one may ride only on a parent's or guardian's land or in an organized event, or from 12 with an off-highway vehicle safety certificate
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a safety helmet meeting US DOT standards
Carries a passenger only if the manufacturer equips and recommends it for one
Kept off the roadway, shoulder and inside slope of roads except as the chapter allows, and out of controlled-access highway rights of way except in emergencies

A registered one may use gravel or dirt roads, and paved highways posted 55 mph or less, only with a mirror, horn, speedometer, odometer, brake light, headlamp and a motor of at least 350 cc, and only if it can reach 30 mph
Needs a working muffler, and may not be ridden on private land posted against trespassing
